We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $u\cdot (2u),$ we multiply $u\cdot u$ by $2.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (2u) & =2(u\cdot u) \\  & =2\cdot 17 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (\frac{1}{3}v),$ we compute $u\cdot v$ first and then multiply the result by $\frac{1}{3}.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (\frac{1}{3}v) & =\frac{1}{3}({u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((0)\cdot (1)+3\cdot (-4)+2\cdot 2+2\cdot (-5)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(0-12+4-10) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-18) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{u\cdot (2u)}{u\cdot (\frac{1}{3}v)}=\frac{34}{-6}=-\frac{17}{3}.
$$
